notes:
Deleting the piston you just placed frees its number again.

**Place 12, place 13, delete 13 — the next one is 13 again**, not 14. In 2.03 the counter stayed where it was, so a deleted number was skipped. It now steps back, but only when the piston you delete is the one you just placed: deleting an older piston leaves the sequence alone, and a number on one memory level is not the same number on another.

It steps back rather than starting over from the highest number on the page, which matters if you have renumbered downwards — delete a freshly placed 250 while an old 320 is still there and starting over would offer you 321 again, which is the behaviour 2.03 was meant to end.

Deleting a whole ink layer resets the sequence outright, since there is no last-placed piston left to carry on from.

Everything else in 2.03 is unchanged; see its notes if you skipped it.
